symptom: A message a business event service both publishes and consumes could only be written by declaring it twice (publish, then subscribe): check, exec and mx check passed, and mxbuild --target=deploy failed: 'Extension BusinessEvents deployment failed! System.ArgumentException: An item with the same key has already been added. Key: AgentMessage' (measured 11.12.6, BusinessEvents 3.12.0). Re-running its describe re-minted a channel name every time.
file: mdl/grammar/domains/MDLService.g4 businessEventMessageDef / businessEventOperationDef / businessEventConsumeDef; mdl/visitor/visitor_businessevents.go businessEventMessageOperations (aliases MDL-DEPR075/076); mdl/executor/cmd_businessevents.go businessEventServiceModel / businessEventMessageProblems / operationOf. Test: mdl/executor/business_event_publish_subscribe_2490_test.go
cause: MDL had one operation per message, so the only way to state both was two messages of one name; the carry handed out stored operations by message name alone.
insight: **mx check is not the last gate: run the deployment build when the failure is reported at deploy.** mxbuild --target=deploy (with --java-home/--java-exe-path) reproduces the Business Events extension's own check headlessly; mx check passed both shapes. The fix is R2's shape, not a new keyword combination: the operations are the message's children, `{ publish (Entity: P); subscribe (Entity: C, Microflow: H); }`, one Message with both flags and two operations. A first cut, `publish subscribe entity P entity C`, gave the second entity meaning by position; R2 (and MDL-DEPR070, which moved REST operations from braces to parentheses) says properties are named, in ( ). Carry operations by (message, operation), or the second operation re-mints and the re-run is never Unchanged.
